producer_report.summary:
I made failure classes deduplicated at creation and mergeable. One shared rule, `introspect::class_named`, now decides when a new class name duplicates an existing live class. It lowercases, keeps only letters and digits, and joins words with one space. When the model answers `new` with such a name, the introspection records the existing class id and adds no class record. `athena review --new-class` uses the same rule and refuses, naming the class to use. It used to compare lower case only, so punctuation slipped through. A merge is a new append-only `athena.failure-class/1` record with status `merged` and `merged_into` / `merged_from` fields. The retired class's file is not touched, and `proposed` records parse as before. `Athena::merge_classes(from, into)` writes the merge record. It refuses a self-merge, an unknown id, a merge record, or an already-retired class. Readers resolve merges in memory: the registry shows live classes only, and a merged class's cases count under the target. The same resolution applies to Hestia's recurrence keys, the producer brief's class summaries, the recurrence evidence label, default proposals and the labeled set. `athena review --class` now refuses a merge record's id and a retired id.

The docs (defaults-loop.md section 3.4, CHANGELOG, decision D166) say that creation-time reuse catches only names equal after normalising. They also say the existing 158 classes are not rewritten, and mark the CLI command, collision backtest, migration and model clustering as design. The full suite passed except `xtask --test spec` (details below).

Beyond the nine listed deliverables I also edited review.rs, proposals.rs, evidence_labels.rs, briefs.rs and the CLI review test. The plan called for these: without them the producer brief would list merge records as classes, and review would apply a weaker name rule.

One failure remains, in `xtask --test spec`: 6 tests fail on BRIEF.md addenda with no requirement in the spec. I changed neither file, so it looks like it comes from the base commit.

open_issues: cargo test --locked fails in xtask --test spec (6 tests: the_real_spec_covers_every_heading_and_addendum_of_the_brief and five related) because BRIEF.md addenda dated 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-08 have no requirement in the spec. None of my files touch BRIEF.md or the spec, so this should come from the base commit, but I could not run a baseline to confirm it. If Athena's full test run fails only there, it is not from this change.
The plan listed 'a CLI merge command' as design only; none was added. The merge path is called only from code and tests until a command exists.
Creation-time reuse catches only names equal after normalising. Differently worded duplicates, and the existing 158 classes, still need merge records. The docs, CHANGELOG and D166 say so.
Departure from the plan: review.rs's Verdict::Right also resolves a retired class to its target (one line, not in the plan), so a label never names a retired id.
Not measured: how many existing classes share a normalised name. records/ is not in the working copy.
mistakes: My first labeled.rs test used the wrong class description, so the registry equality failed; fixed by using the description the shared classes() helper expects.
In the first full workspace run I could not see the failing target because the output was truncated; I reran with --no-fail-fast and --quiet to find it.
learnings: Records are append-only, so a merge has to be a new failure-class record; ClassStatus::Merged { merged_into, merged_from } needed no new field on FailureClass, so no struct literal elsewhere changed.
store::Records.classes (athena-core) and introspect::Records.all_classes both include merge records; every reader that lists or counts classes has to go through ClassMerges.
Cases are read before classes in introspect::read_records, so I moved the class read ahead of the introspection loop so CaseRow.failure_class can be resolved.
The labeled.rs test the_scoring_path_never_opens_a_file_for_writing scans the non-test source for write-like substrings; new code there must avoid them.
xtask --test spec fails in this snapshot because BRIEF.md has addenda (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-08) with no requirement in the spec, independent of this job.
desires: A baseline run of the full suite at the base commit, to confirm the xtask spec failure is not from my change.
records/ in the working copy, to count how many real classes share a normalised name.
